 Karl-Anthony Towns accounted for 28 points (10-of-21 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 17 rebounds, three assists, one steal and three three-pointers in Sunday’s win over the Raptors.
 Towns extended his season-opening streak of games with a double-double to 13 on Sunday, and the Knicks needed every contribution. New York trailed by 13 with less than nine minutes remaining in the fourth quarter, then rallied to take the lead late in regulation. New York needed overtime to extend their win streak over Toronto to 14 games, and KAT had a lot to do with that. The Knicks play four games next week, starting with the Raptors again on Tuesday. 
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Karl-Anthony Towns recorded 23 points (9-of-19 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 15 rebounds, five assists, three steals and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the Pacers. 
 Towns has now recorded a double-double in each of the Knicks’ first 12 games, breaking the franchise record for the longest double-double streak to begin a season, previously held by Willis Reed. He had a chance to force overtime, but his fadeaway fell short as time expired. Along with Jalen Brunson, Towns has been one of the few constants for the Knicks in their 6-6 start. He’ll look to extend his double-double streak on Sunday against the Raptors.

 Karl-Anthony Towns recorded 21 points (7-of-11 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), 11 rebounds, eight assists, one block and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Cavaliers. 
 Another game, another double-double for Towns, who’s up to 11 for the season. KAT finished Wednesday’s defeat two assists shy of a triple-double and shot the ball well from the field and the foul line. Towns is closing in on being a first-round player in nine-cat formats, which is about where most fantasy managers selected him in drafts.

 Karl-Anthony Towns accumulated 21 points (5-of-14 FGs, 9-of-14 FTs), 16 rebounds, three assists, two steals, one block and two three-pointers in Tuesday’s win over the Bucks. 
 Towns didn’t shoot the ball well from the field or the foul line, but that didn’t eliminate all of his fantasy value. As has been the case all season, KAT was dominant on the glass, corralling a game-high 16 rebounds. Add in the assists and defensive contributions, and this was a good start to Towns’ four-game week. As a team, the Knicks outrebounded the Bucks 70-34, with Andre Drummond joining Towns in double figures with 14 rebounds.

 Karl-Anthony Towns amassed 29 points (11-of-21 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), 13 rebounds, three assists, two steals and two three-pointers in Saturday’s win over the Cavaliers. 
 Towns shouldered most of the Knicks’ offensive workload in the first quarter, scoring 14 points. Having recorded a double-double in each of the Knicks’ first nine games, KAT finished Saturday’s victory with a season-high point total. Also, Towns’ 21 shot attempts matched his season high. Tuesday’s game against the Bucks may be another opportunity for Towns to put up a gaudy stat line.

 Karl-Anthony Towns accumulated 17 points (5-of-5 FGs, 5-of-7 FTs), 12 rebounds, one assist, one steal and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Bulls. 
 Towns, who didn’t miss a shot from the field, attempted just five shots on Wednesday. The Knicks center has recorded a double-double in all eight games this season and is providing third-round value in 12-team leagues. Fantasy managers likely want to see a little more from Towns defensively, but he’s gotten this season off to a solid start.

 Karl-Anthony Towns finished Monday’s win over the Nets with 11 points (4-of-11 FGs, 2-of-3 FTs), 16 rebounds, five assists and one three-pointer. 
 Although Towns failed to score in the first half, missing all four shots, he remained active on the boards. KAT grabbed 10 of his 16 rebounds before halftime, and the Knicks made a more concerted effort to get him the ball in the third quarter. Towns scored nine points in the third quarter, and he finished the game with his seventh double-double in as many games.

 Karl-Anthony Towns tallied 22 points (8-of-15 FGs, 3-of-3 FTs), 12 rebounds, three assists, one block and three three-pointers in Friday’s loss to the 76ers. 
 Towns has recorded a double-double in each of the Knicks’ six games this season, and he committed no fouls in Friday’s defeat. Given his occasional struggles with foul trouble, KAT avoiding it in a matchup with Philadelphia’s Joel Embiid is noteworthy. Unfortunately for managers rostering Towns, the Knicks don’t play again this week. But they do host the Nets on Monday.

 Amen Thompson recorded a team-high 26 points (9-of-11 FGs, 5-of-6 FTs), seven rebounds, seven assists, one steal and one block over 29 minutes to power the Rockets to a 147-119 blowout win over the Wizards on Sunday.
 Thompson had a real shot at a triple-double on a night where Houston shot nearly 60 percent from the floor, including 45 percent (15-of-333) from three-point range to cruise to a nearly 30-point victory. He scored 19 first-half points and broke the 20-point threshold for the first time since October 28. He’s still not a threat from three-point range, but he did knock down a season-high three of them in this one. He’s managed to deliver early-round fantasy value this season, averaging 15.8 points, 7.0 rebounds, 3.4 assists, 1.1 steals and 0.7 blocks through 14 games. The Rockets have a three-game week on tap that features road tilts against the Heat, Pacers and Nuggets.
 -  George Bissell

 Alex Sarr finished with 25 points (9-of-13 FGs, 4-of-8 FTs), nine rebounds, two assists and three blocks over 27 minutes in Sunday’s loss to the Rockets.
 Sarr came into this one questionable due to illness and didn’t appear to be limited early on as he dropped a team-high 15 points on 6-of-8 shooting in the opening half. He’s put together his best stretch of the season recently, scoring at least 25 points while also corralling nine boards in back-to-back contests. He also has four blocks during that span. The Wizards have a busy four-game week coming up with showdowns against the Grizzlies, Raptors, Bulls and Magic.
 -  George Bissell

 Kevin Durant accumulated 25 points (8-of-13 FGs, 7-of-8 FTs), four rebounds, five assists and one steal over 30 minutes in Sunday’s lopsided win over the Wizards.
 Durant didn’t hold back against his hometown Wizards, dropping 16 first-half points on a night where everything was going in for Houston. He was barely needed in the second half as the Rockets erupted for 46 points in the third quarter and pulled away for a near 40-point victory. One of the most prolific scoring forwards ever, Durant has topped 20 points in six consecutive games. The Rockets will carry a four-game winning streak into a three-game week that features road tilts against the Heat, Pacers and Nuggets.
 -  George Bissell

 Anthony Davis posted 14 points (4-of-11 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), eight rebounds, five assists, one steal and two blocks over 31 minutes in Sunday’s one-sided defeat at the hands of the Rockets.
 Davis came into this one having eclipsed 20 points in six consecutive games and seven of his last eight overall. It was just the fifth time all season that he failed to post double-digit rebounds. He likely would’ve gotten there had Washington not fallen behind by nearly 40 points in the second half. He’s authored a phenomenal campaign in his Wizards debut, delivering first-round fantasy value by averaging nearly 25 points and 11 rebounds through 12 games. The Wizards have a four-game week on tap with matchups against the Grizzlies, Raptors, Bulls and Magic.
 -  George Bissell

 Alperen Şengün tallied 19 points (5-of-8 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), eight rebounds, eight assists and two steals over 29 minutes in Sunday’s blowout win over the Wizards.
 Şengün finished just shy of a triple-double as he occupied more of a connector role in this one with Amen Thompson and Kevin Durant catching fire. His eight shot attempts were his lowest single-game total of the entire season by a considerable margin. He still managed to make an impact by dishing out eight assists and grabbing eight boards. He’s averaging 22.8 points, 9.5 rebounds, 7.7 assists, 1.2 steals and 1.0 blocks through 12 games. The Rockets are back in action with a three-game week that features road showdowns against the Heat, Pacers and Nuggets.

 Eason got some additional run with Houston opening up a massive cushion in this one and he managed to cross the 20-point threshold for the first time this season. He shot 71 percent from the floor, including 3-of-5 from three-point range, and chipped in seven rebounds as well. He’s more of a fringe fantasy option than anything else, but he’s capable of taking advantage of favorable matchups like this one.
